business_summary: Meta Platforms is classed as an internet platforms company. Revenue grew at a 19.89% annual rate over three years to FY25 and 18.51% over five years. FY25 operating margin was 50.7%, up 18.43 percentage points in three years. Borrowings are modest at 0.27 times equity, and none of the last four quarters was loss-making.
why_own: The case rests on fast revenue growth (19.89% a year over 3 years) converting into very high profitability (50.7% operating margin, 31.56% ROCE) with cash profit well above reported profit (1.92x). The valuation (23.74x trailing earnings, 8.22x book) already reflects much of this, so the thesis depends on growth and margins holding. No investor documents were supplied, so the drivers are quantitative only.

drivers.statement: Revenue keeps compounding at a double-digit rate; the 3-year CAGR is 19.89% today. (warn line tightened by code from 12 to 13.92.)
Operating margin stays near its current 50.7% level after expanding 18.43 percentage points over three years.
Returns on capital stay high; ROCE is 31.56% and ROE is 30.24%. (warn line tightened by code from 22 to 22.09.)
Reported profit is backed by cash; operating cash flow is 1.92 times net profit. (warn line tightened by code from 1.2 to 1.34.)

kill_criteria.description: Operating margin falls below 30%, which would undo most of the three-year margin expansion.
3-year revenue CAGR falls below 7%, a sharp slowdown from 19.89% today.
Debt to equity rises above 1.0x, well beyond today's 0.27x.

risks.statement: Valuation leaves limited room for disappointment: the stock trades at 23.74x trailing earnings and 8.22x book. Its P/E comparison with its own 5-year history is not available, so whether this is rich or cheap against its past is untested.
The 50.7% operating margin is up 18.43 percentage points in three years. A reversal of part of that gain would hit profit growth hard, and the evidence does not show how durable the gain is.
Trailing four-quarter net profit (75,249 USD m) is well above FY25 net profit (60,458 USD m). Whether that step-up is sustainable is untested by the evidence provided.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis is wrong if the 50.7% margin is a cyclical peak rather than a new base. Kill line K1 (30%) sits below the pre-expansion level of about 32% (50.7 minus 18.43pp), so margins could erase the whole gain before the thesis counts as broken. The D2 warn line of 40% allows a drop of over 10pp. The 3-year revenue CAGR is a lagging metric, and its break line of 8% is far below the current 19.89%. At 23.74x earnings and 8.22x book, the price assumes both hold. The earnings base is also unclear: trailing profit of 75,249 is far above FY25 profit of 60,458, though both are labelled to Dec 2025. What would change this view: Evidence that operating margin has stayed above about 45% through a slowdown in quarterly revenue growth, together with a reconciliation of why trailing profit (75,249) exceeds FY25 profit (60,458), would drop my objection.
